name: Yankee Tea Cakes
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: fresh butter
ingredients.originalText: half a pound of fresh butter

ingredients.name: powdered white sugar
ingredients.originalText: half a pound of powdered white sugar

ingredients.name: jill of strong fresh yeast
ingredients.originalText: half a jill of strong fresh yeast

instructions.text: Cut up half a pound of fresh butter in a pint of milk and warm it a little, so as to soften but not melt the butter
Add, gradually, half a pound of powdered white sugar, in turn with three well-beaten eggs and a pound of sifted flour, finishing with half a jill of strong fresh yeast
Set the mixture in a warm place to rise
When it has risen high and the top is covered with bubbles, butter some cups and bake it in them about twenty minutes
When done, turn the cakes out on large plates, send them to table hot, and split and butter them

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. Cut up half a pound of fresh butter in a pint of milk and warm it a little, so as to soften but not melt the butter
2. Add, gradually, half a pound of powdered white sugar, in turn with three well-beaten eggs and a pound of sifted flour, finishing with half a jill of strong fresh yeast
3. Set the mixture in a warm place to rise
4. When it has risen high and the top is covered with bubbles, butter some cups and bake it in them about twenty minutes
5. When done, turn the cakes out on large plates, send them to table hot, and split and butter them
